definitions.explanation: An electric charge that builds up on the surface of objects, commonly experienced as a small shock when touching metal objects or other people, especially in dry winter weather.

examples.japanese: {静電気|せいでんき}⟦で→で：00502_de⟧バチッときた。
⟦{冬|ふゆ}→冬：00623_fuyu⟧⟦は→は：00079_ha⟧{静電気|せいでんき}⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧⟦{起|お}き→起きる：00521_okiru⟧やすい。
examples.english: Static electricity occurs easily in winter.

examples.japanese: ドアノブ⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧⟦{触|さわ}る→触る：00808_sawaru⟧たび⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧{静電気|せいでんき}⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧⟦{走|はし}る→走る：00519_hashiru⟧⟦の→の：09472_no⟧で⟦{困|こま}っている→困る：00861_komaru⟧。
examples.english: I'm bothered by getting a static shock every time I touch a doorknob.

notes: Combines {静|せい} (still, static) + ⟦{電気|でんき}→電気：09780_denki⟧ (electricity). Very commonly discussed in Japan during the dry winter months. Common collocations: {静電気|せいでんき}⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧⟦{起|お}きる→起きる：00521_okiru⟧ (static builds up), {静電気|せいでんき}⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧⟦{走|はし}る→走る：00519_hashiru⟧ (a static shock runs through), {静電気|せいでんき}⟦{防止|ぼうし}→防止：14571_boushi⟧ (anti-static), {静電気|せいでんき}⟦{除去|じょきょ}→除去：14567_jokyo⟧ (static removal). Products like {静電気|せいでんき}⟦{防止|ぼうし}→防止：14571_boushi⟧⟦スプレー→スプレー：11581_supuree⟧ (anti-static spray) are popular in Japan.
